props.title: Read One Aloud

B34.visual_intent: Act title 'Read One Aloud' (serif 40) top-left. The 14-line file alone on the stage, line numbers prominent (the next beats say 'line three', 'line six'). A focus box rests on line 1, then moves to line 3 where the reading will start.
B34.motion_claim: The focus box leaves the header and settles on line three, ready to read.
B34.why: The file with its line numbers is the stage for the next eight beats; ShaderLab shows all 14 lines at once.

B35.visual_intent: Two lines in monospace (size 36), lines 3 and 4 of the file: `uniform vec4 tint : source_color;` and `uniform float speed = 2.0;`. Drawn tags land beneath their pieces: under `uniform` 'set from outside'; under `vec4` 'a color'; a bracket under `: source_color` labelled 'hint' with a small outlined round swatch and the label 'treated as a color'; a tag at the end of line 3 'no default: black'; under `float` 'a decimal number'; a bracket under `= 2.0` labelled 'default'. Serif 32 caption, in the GLOSSARY wording: 'hint: the word after a colon that tells Godot how to treat a uniform'.
B35.motion_claim: Tags fly out to the pieces of line three, then to the pieces of line four, as each is read.

show.event: line three; uniform and vec4 tags
line four: float and default tags

B35.runner_up: ShaderLab with a label per cue
B35.why: Each piece of two real lines gets its own small tag in place; the whole-file panel can only label a line as a whole.

B36.visual_intent: Line 6 `vec3 breathe(vec3 base, float t) {` in monospace (size 36), centered. Drawn tags land beneath: `vec3` 'hands back a vec3'; `breathe` 'name'; `vec3 base` 'argument: vec3'; `float t` 'argument: float'. Below, a small three-cell token and a one-cell token flow into the parentheses and a three-cell token leaves, with the note 'the body must return a vec3'.
B36.motion_claim: Tags land on the four pieces of the signature, then a token flows through.

show.event: tokens in and out; must return vec3

B36.runner_up: ShaderLab with a label per cue
B36.why: The same four pieces of one real line, read in place.

B37.visual_intent: Line 7 `float wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(t);` in monospace (size 36). Nested drawn brackets from the inside out with tags: `t` float; `sin(t)` float; `0.5 * sin(t)` float; `0.5 + 0.5 * sin(t)` float; into `wave` float. At the right (or below), a small drawn sine curve on axes marked -1 and 1, then squeezed and lifted to span 0 to 1, with a dot riding the curve.
B37.motion_claim: Brackets widen outward with a float tag on each; a sine curve is squeezed from -1..1 into 0..1.

show.event: brackets and float tags, inside out
the sine curve squeezed into 0 to 1

B37.why: The range change from -1..1 to 0..1 is a curve being squeezed and lifted; the tags show the type never leaves float.

B38.visual_intent: Line 8 `return mix(vec3(0.9), base, wave);` in monospace (size 36). Tags: `vec3(0.9)` 'fills all three: a pale gray' with a small gray swatch; `base` 'vec3'; `wave` 'float: 0 to 1'; the whole `mix(...)` 'vec3'; `return` 'matches the signature'. A serif 32 label in the GLOSSARY wording, 'mix(a, b, t): blends from a to b: t of 0 gives a, 1 gives b'. Below, a horizontal ramp strip from pale gray (left) to teal (right) with a terracotta dot that rides from the gray end to the teal end as wave goes from 0 to 1, labelled '0 gives the gray, 1 gives base'.
B38.motion_claim: A dot rides a gray-to-teal ramp as wave goes from zero to one while the tags land on the pieces.

show.event: vec3(0.9) tag and swatch; base; wave
dot rides the ramp from gray to teal

B38.runner_up: ShaderLab with a label per cue
B38.why: The ramp strip with a riding marker is the series' picture of a blend; the tags show the types fit.

B39.visual_intent: Lines 12 and 13 in monospace (size 32): `vec3 color = breathe(tint.rgb, TIME * speed);` (45 characters) and `COLOR = vec4(color, tint.a);`. Tags land inside out: `tint.rgb` vec3 (swizzle); `TIME * speed` float; `breathe(...)` vec3; into `color` vec3; then `vec4(color, tint.a)` vec4 into `COLOR`, a vec4. Captions in serif 32: 'TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game' and 'COLOR: the color of the pixel being drawn; fragment() sets it'.
B39.motion_claim: Tags land inside out on line twelve, then on line thirteen, ending on COLOR.
B39.runner_up: ShaderLab with a label per cue
B39.why: Two real lines read inside out, with the types landing on each piece, are the film's method applied.

B40.runner_up: manim: the file with all tags at once

props.title: Godot 4.7.2 · shader compile error · printed by the engine
lines: SHADER ERROR: Invalid member for 'vec3' expression: '.a'.

B41.visual_intent: A terminal window with the engine's own log of lab-shaders/57-err-alpha-on-vec3.gdshader (the same file with the uniform changed to `vec3 tint`), word for word: the source lines around `COLOR = vec4(color, tint.a);` with that line marked, then 'Invalid member for 'vec3' expression: '.a'.' A ring lands on the message.
B41.motion_claim: The log lands line by line; a ring settles on the message about the missing member.
B41.why: The film's method pays off as a caught mistake; the engine's own words are the proof.
